declined.reason: 倶利加羅紋々 is tattoo slang for heavily tattooed men in general, not a name for the specific dragon or hannya described in p48; importing 'kurikara' would add a Japanese term the house style does not keep and would specify what the text leaves general.

'Me, I've got...' would fake the 俺-to-僕 slide with broken English the Japanese does not have; the slide cannot be shown with English pronouns, and the loss is already visible in the translator's note rather than in a caricature.

一ト息 in p43 is not the slogan 一気呵勢; the bible fixes 'in one burst!' for the slogan itself, and giving the workmen's 'one more push' of breath the slogan's words would invent a migration the Japanese words do not make.
As with F9, 一ト息 is a literal breath spent herding the carp, distinct from 一気呵勢; 'in one breath' keeps that distinction while the echo remains audible.

Accepted in part ('the talk lapsed', and 'sash' kept per the style sheet rather than 'obi sash'); declined on the '(?)', which is in the Japanese after 'difficult pieces' as the narrator's own ironic query, not a proof mark.
Accepted in part (the piled 'comfortable' dropped); declined 'landsman' and 'sound', since 安逸の素面 names no landsman and the Japanese says the chorus would look forced, not sound so.

The Japanese itself breaks the slogan off as 「一気――な」仕事, one more unfinished thing; completing it to 'in one burst' would supply what the text cuts short, and the half-phrase is recognisable from p28 and p74.

disagreements.choice: Removed the 'I': 'Whether admirable or timid, when it comes to money this man never runs up any debt...' with the muttering then tied to the wife as she rises.
disagreements.faithful_side: F6: the Japanese leaves the knower of 感心なのか、臆病なのか知らないが indefinite, and this narration never elsewhere says 'I', so the inserted first person breaks the even third-person voice.
disagreements.readable_side: R11: keep the 'I do not know' but repair the dangling participle so the judging 'I' and the muttering wife no longer trade places.

disagreements.choice: Left both 一ト息 passages as breath/push rather than the slogan, as above.
disagreements.faithful_side: F9 and F10: unify 一息 with 一気呵勢 as 'burst' so the slogan's migration into the pond work, and its throwing-back in p160, stays visible.
disagreements.readable_side: No readable note on these lines; the translator's draft keeps 一息 apart from the fixed slogan, as a literal single breath in the work at hand.

data.say:
Declined: F4 (倶利加羅紋々 is general tattoo slang, not the p48 motif by name, and 'kurikara' would import a term the style sheet does not keep); F8 (the suggested 'me, I've got...' fakes the 俺/僕 slide with broken English — the slide cannot be carried by English pronouns and is already flagged in the translator's note); F9 and F10 (一ト息 is not 一気呵勢 — see disagreements); R15 (see below). Accepted in part only: R8 ('the talk lapsed' taken; 'obi sash' declined for the style sheet's 'sash', and the '(?)' kept because it stands in the Japanese as the narrator's ironic query, not a proof mark) and R10 ('comfortable' dropped; 'landsman' and 'sound' declined as neither is in 安逸の素面から口吟まれれば...見える). All other notes were taken, in the smallest form that did the job, including F13 rendered literally as 'The Blacksmith in the Forest' rather than the suggested 'The Village Blacksmith', which would identify the piece as a different, named work on no evidence in the text.

Disagreements and unsettled places:

1. p119 (F6 against R11). Faithful: remove the first-person 'I do not know', which the Japanese never supplies and which breaks the even third-person narration. Readable: keep the 'I' and fix only the dangling participle. Choice: the faithful side — the 'I' is gone and the sentence now runs 'Whether admirable or timid, when it comes to money this man...', with the muttering tied to the wife as she rises. The narration's person, as the bible and reading settle it, is third-person throughout, so this does not go up.

2. p43 and p177 (F9/F10, against the draft and, in effect, between the two cruxes). Faithful: 一息 should be Englished as 'burst' so Taki's slogan visibly migrates into the pond work. Other side: 一ト息 is a literal breath, a different word from 一気呵勢, and the fixed concordance the bible mandates covers the slogan, not every breath in the book. Choice: keep the words distinct ('one more push' stands in p43, 'in one breath' in p177). This goes up to the editor: the two readings pull different ways on how rigid the slogan family should be, the notes themselves ask the editor to decide whether 一息 belongs to it, and being wrong would dull either a real echo or a real distinction.

3. p208 (R15, readable against the text's own truncation). Readable: 'in one— work' is unintelligible and the full slogan should be restored. Other side: the Japanese breaks the phrase off itself, 「一気――な」仕事, in a story built of unfinished things, and the fragment is recognisable from p28 and p74. Choice: stet. The reading's insistence on leaving unfinished things unfinished settles it, so it does not go up.

Nothing in this part changes how an earlier part should read.

House log: The desk took twenty-six notes, declined the pronoun-slide and kurikara fixes and the 一息 unification (the last sent up as a fork), and held the money, tattoo and slogan concordances against domestication.
